levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: Some criteria are used and others are dropped without saying why.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: Every stated criterion is applied and the result of each is reported.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: Every criterion is applied and the response says which one decided the outcome.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The response says the work is wrong but not where or why.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The response locates the first wrong step and states the misconception behind it.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The response locates the error, names the misconception, and gives a check that would have caught it.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The parts of the plan contradict each other or do not add up.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up but one part is not connected to the rest.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up and each part is consistent with the others and with the constraint.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up, is internally consistent, and states what would break it first.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: A choice is asserted with no cost acknowledged.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: A choice is defended but what it gives up is not named.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended and what it costs or forecloses is named specifically.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended, its cost is named, and the strongest case against it is answered.

judgment.prompt: The rule requires selling $1,353.60 of the fund that returned 21.4% to buy more of the one that returned 2.6%. Explain what the rule is protecting against, and say why writing it in advance is part of how it works.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Explains that without rebalancing the portfolio drifts towards whatever has risen, so its risk profile changes by accident rather than by decision — here from 60% to 64.0% in stocks.
Explains that a rule written before the drift removes the judgement at the moment it is hardest, when selling the strong performer feels wrong.
Notes that the rule is mechanical: it is triggered by the 3 percentage point threshold rather than by a view about what will happen next.
evidenceRequirements: Cites the 64.0% drifted weight against the 60% target and the $1,353.60 trade it implies.
lookFors: The response identifies unintended drift in risk as the thing being protected against.
The response treats the advance commitment as the mechanism, not merely as good organisation.
The response does not claim rebalancing improves returns; it manages the mix.
judgment.commonMisconception: Reading rebalancing as an attempt to predict which holding will do better next.

judgment.prompt: The target is 60% of $34,164.00, not the original $18,000.00. Explain why the target moves with the portfolio, and what would go wrong if it did not.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Explains that the policy sets a share of the portfolio, so the dollar target rises and falls with the total — 60% of the new total is $20,498.40.
States what a fixed dollar target would do: after a strong year it would force selling far more than the drift requires, and after a poor year it would push the mix away from the intended shares.
evidenceRequirements: Uses the $20,498.40 target and the $18,000.00 starting holding in the explanation.
lookFors: The response distinguishes a share target from a dollar target.
The consequence described follows from the arithmetic.

nonDiagnosticGuard: Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
